The Best One-Pot Lemon Chicken Orzo

By Giulia · Updated 12 September 2026 · 48 comments

Every summer my nonna would open the windows of her kitchen in Liguria and the whole street would know what was for dinner. I still remember the smell of lemons on her hands. She never measured anything, and somehow it came out perfect every single time.

This recipe has been on my list for years, and honestly I don't know why it took me so long to share it with you. It has become a weeknight staple in our house, and my kids ask for it at least twice a week. There is something magical about a dish that comes together in one pot while the pasta water never even has to boil.

If you make it, please tag me on Instagram, I love seeing your photos! Be sure to scroll down for the printable recipe card and a few reader questions I've answered below. I've partnered with my favourite olive oil brand this month, and you can get 15% off with my code.

Sponsored: try the new Ligurian Gold extra virgin olive oil, now with free shipping on your first order.

A quick word on the chicken. Boneless thighs stay juicy through the long simmer, and the skin renders enough fat that you barely need oil. Breasts work too, but cut the simmer by three minutes or they will dry out.

Ingredients

  • 500 g boneless chicken thighs, skin on
  • 300 g of dried orzo pasta
  • 1 lemon
  • 750 ml of hot chicken stock
  • 2 cloves of garlic, finely sliced
  • 1 tablespoon of olive oil
  • A handful of flat-leaf parsley, chopped
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper

Method

  1. Season the chicken generously on both sides. Sear it skin-side down in a wide pan for 6 minutes without moving it, or it will not brown.
  2. Turn the chicken, add the garlic and cook for one minute more until fragrant.
  3. Add the orzo and stir for one minute so it toasts slightly before the stock goes in. This step matters more than it looks: toasted orzo keeps its bite, holds the sauce better, and gives the whole dish a faintly nutty depth that you will miss if you skip it, so do not rush it even when everyone is hungry and asking when dinner is ready.
  4. Pour in the stock, bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 12 to 14 minutes, stirring every few minutes so the orzo does not stick to the bottom.
  5. Take the pan off the heat before adding the lemon juice, or the sauce will turn bitter.
  6. Scatter over the parsley and serve straight from the pan.

Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to three days; add a splash of stock when reheating. I would not freeze this one, the orzo goes mushy.
